questions.question: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is G.V. Mavalankar.

Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar served as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha from 1952 to 1956.

  • He was also the Speaker of the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) from 1946 to 1950.
  • He was a freedom fighter and a member of the Indian National Congress.
  • He established many parliamentary conventions in India.

questions.question: The first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sucheta Kriplani.

Sucheta Kriplani became the first woman Chief Minister of India in Uttar Pradesh from 1963 to 1967.

  • She was a freedom fighter and a member of the Constituent Assembly.
  • She sang 'Vande Mataram' in the Constituent Assembly on August 14, 1947.
  • She was also the founder of the women's wing of Congress.

questions.question: The first woman Governor of an Indian state was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sarojini Naidu.

Sarojini Naidu became the first woman Governor of India in Uttar Pradesh from 1947 to 1949.

  • She was also the first Indian woman president of the Indian National Congress.
  • She was given the title 'Nightingale of India' by Mahatma Gandhi.
  • Her birthday (February 13) is celebrated as 'National Women's Day'.

questions.question: The first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection of poems 'Gitanjali'.

  • He was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
  • C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.
  • Tagore also composed the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: The first Indian to win the Bharat Ratna award was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.

The Bharat Ratna was first awarded in 1954 to three individuals:

  • Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (first Vice President and second President of India)
  • C. Rajagopalachari (last Governor-General of India)
  • Dr. C.V. Raman (Nobel laureate in Physics)

questions.question: The first Indian to win the Magsaysay Award was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Acharya Vinoba Bhave.

Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1958 for his Bhoodan Movement.

  • He was a spiritual leader and follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
  • He was also the first individual to be awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously (1983).
  • The Magsaysay Award is often called 'Asia's Nobel Prize'.

questions.question: The first Indian to receive the Oscar Award was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhanu Athaiya.

Bhanu Athaiya won the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Costume Design for the film 'Gandhi' (1982).

  • She was the first Indian to win an Oscar.
  • Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar in 1992.
  • A.R. Rahman and Resul Pookutty won Oscars in 2009 for 'Slumdog Millionaire'.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to go into space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rakesh Sharma.

Squadron Leader Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian to go into space in April 1984 aboard the Soviet rocket Soyuz T-11.

  • He was awarded the Ashoka Chakra and Hero of the Soviet Union.
  • When asked by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi how India looked from space, he famously replied, 'Sare Jahan Se Achha'.
  • Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space (1997).

questions.question: The first nuclear test conducted by India was code-named:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Smiling Buddha.

India's first nuclear test was conducted on May 18, 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan.

  • The code name was 'Smiling Buddha'.
  • The second series of nuclear tests (1998) was code-named 'Operation Shakti'.
  • India became a nuclear weapon state after the 1998 tests.

questions.question: The first satellite launched by India was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Aryabhata.

Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on April 19, 1975 from Kapustin Yar.

  • It was named after the ancient Indian mathematician Aryabhata.
  • It was designed and built by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation).
  • Rohini was the first satellite launched by an Indian launch vehicle (SLV-3) in 1980.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Program'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vikram Sarabhai.

Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Program'.

  • He founded the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in 1969.
  • The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) in Thiruvananthapuram is named after him.
  • He also established the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) in Ahmedabad.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win the Booker Prize?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Salman Rushdie.

Salman Rushdie won the Booker Prize in 1981 for his novel 'Midnight's Children'.

  • V.S. Naipaul (born in Trinidad) won the Booker Prize in 1971.
  • Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for 'The God of Small Things'.
  • The 'Booker of Bookers' prize (1993) was also awarded to 'Midnight's Children'.

questions.question: The first Indian woman to win the Booker Prize was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for her debut novel 'The God of Small Things'.

  • She was the first Indian woman to win the Booker Prize.
  • She is also a political activist and documentary filmmaker.
  • Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize in 2006 for 'The Inheritance of Loss'.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Syed Ahmed Khan.

The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha was a social reform organization founded in 1851 by Parsis in Bombay.

  • It was composed of Dadabhai Naoroji, J.B. Wacha, S.S. Bengalee, and Naoroji Furdonji.
  • It was funded by K.N. Kama.
  • Syed Ahmed Khan was associated with the Aligarh Movement, not this Sabha.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct about Prarthana Samaj?
A. Prarthana Samaj or Prayer Society in Sanskrit, was a movement for religious and social reforms.
B. Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1863 by Dadoba Pandurang and his brother Atmaram Pandurang.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only A.

  • Statement A is correct: Prarthana Samaj (Prayer Society) was a movement for religious and social reforms.
  • Statement B is incorrect: The Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay by Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang in 1867, not 1863.

Other members included R.C. Bhandarkar and Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade. Its aims were to remove caste restrictions, abolish child marriage, encourage women's education, and promote widow remarriage.

questions.question: Sree Narayana Guru considered the differences based on caste and religion as meaningless and advocated the principle of 'One Caste, one Religion and one God' for all. He belonged to which of the following organisations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam.

Sree Narayana Guru was a social reformer from Kerala.

  • He built a temple dedicated to Lord Shiva at Aruvippuram in 1888, challenging caste restrictions.
  • He founded the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP Yogam) in 1903.
  • His famous slogan was 'One Caste, One Religion, One God for All'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Kandukuri Veeresalingam pioneered the movement for widow remarriage and girls' education in the Andhra region.
Reason (R): Sree Narayana Guru was regarded as the father of the Telugu Renaissance movement in Andhra Pradesh.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

  • Assertion (A) is true: Kandukuri Veeresalingam (1848-1919) was a social reformer from Andhra Pradesh who pioneered widow remarriage and girls' education.
  • Reason (R) is false: Kandukuri Veeresalingam (not Sree Narayana Guru) is regarded as the 'father of the Telugu Renaissance movement'.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations was founded in Poona, Satara and other towns of Maharashtra that worked against Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Paramahansa Mandali.

  • Paramahansa Mandali was a secret socio-religious group established in 1849 in Bombay.
  • It was closely related to Manav Dharma Sabha, founded in 1844 in Surat.
  • It worked against Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism.

questions.question:
Match the following associations with the class whose interests they primarily represented:
List IList II
1. Landholders' Society (1838)A. Merchants and businessmen
2. Bombay Association (1852)B. Landlords (Zamindars)
3. Madras Native Association (1852)C. Educated middle-class elites
4. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870)D. Political awareness in Madras region
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1-B, 2-A, 3-D, 4-C.

  • Landholders' Society (1838) represented landlords (Zamindars) - founded in Calcutta by Dwarkanath Tagore and others.
  • Bombay Association (1852) represented merchants and businessmen - founded by Dadabhai Naoroji.
  • Madras Native Association (1852) created political awareness in the Madras region.
  • Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) represented educated middle-class elites - founded by M.G. Ranade.

questions.question: Who started the temple entry movement in 1927?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhimrao Ambedkar.

The temple entry movement was started to allow lower caste people to enter temples.

  • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for Dalits' right to drink water from the Chavdar Tank.
  • In 1930, he led the Kalaram Temple entry movement in Nashik.
  • Other leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and V. T. Patil also supported temple entry movements.

questions.question: Visva Bharati a famous educational institute was founded in 1921 by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

Visva-Bharati University was founded by Rabindranath Tagore in 1921 at Santiniketan, West Bengal.

  • It became a central university in 1951.
  • It is known as the 'world's first living heritage university'.
  • Tagore also founded the Santiniketan school in 1901.

questions.question: Who established Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan to promote education and culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. Kanhaiyalal Manekal Munshi.

Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan is a charitable public trust founded on November 7, 1938.

  • Dr. K.M. Munshi was a freedom fighter, writer, and educationist.
  • He also served as the Governor of Uttar Pradesh (1952-1957).
  • The Bhavan has over 100 centers worldwide.

questions.question: Who had founded the first Women's University in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dhondo Keshav Karve (Maharishi Karve).

  • He founded the first women's university in India, SNDT Women's University, in 1916 in Pune.
  • He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (1958) and Padma Vibhushan (1955).
  • The Widow Remarriage Association was founded by Vishnu Shastri Pandit.

questions.question: ______ was the first woman to be accorded the title Pandita by the faculty of Calcutta University for her exceptional knowledge of Sanskrit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ramabai Sarasvati.

Pandita Ramabai was a social reformer and a pioneer in women's education and emancipation.

  • She was the first woman to be awarded the titles of 'Pandita' and 'Sarasvati'.
  • She was one of the 10 women delegates of the Congress session of 1889.
  • She founded the Arya Mahila Samaj to promote women's education.

questions.question: The first session of All India Depressed Classes Congress was held at ______ in 1930.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nagpur.

The first session of the All India Depressed Classes Congress was held in Nagpur in 1930.

  • It was led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
  • He also founded the Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (Outcastes Welfare Association) in 1923.
  • The Poona Pact (1932) was a result of negotiations between Ambedkar and Gandhi.
